stem: A 4-year-old child has unilateral nasal discharge, excoriation at the nostril, and intermittent epistaxis. Which diagnosis should be considered first?
explanation: Nasal foreign body is the most likely diagnosis. This is because unilateral nasal discharge with local excoriation and intermittent epistaxis is a classic presentation in a young child and should prompt this diagnosis first.

citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Correct because unilateral nasal discharge with excoriation and intermittent epistaxis is a classic presentation of a nasal foreign body in a young child.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because viral pharyngitis causes sore throat symptoms rather than unilateral nasal discharge with local trauma and bleeding.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because septal haematoma is usually associated with nasal trauma and obstruction, not isolated unilateral discharge and excoriation.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because juvenile angiofibroma typically presents in adolescent males with recurrent epistaxis, not in a 4-year-old child.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because these findings are abnormal and should not be attributed to a normal nasal examination.
